newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Cullen tips June 19 as budget date - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Cullen tips June 19 as budget date - NZPA.

text.p: New Zealand opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen is tipping June 19 as budget day, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.
Spokesmen for Treasurer Winston Peters and Finance Minister Bill Birch would neither confirm nor deny the date.
A spokesman for Peters said the government would announce the budget date later this month.
Cullen made the suggestion in parliament on Thursday during the second reading of the Treasurer (Statutory References) Bill.
The bill recognises the new position of treasurer, and the split in responsibilities between the treasurer and the minister of finance.
Peters told parliament he wanted the bill referred to the finance and expenditure select committee and reported back to parliament on June 9.
Cullen said this gave "an indication the likely target budget date is the 19th of June" as that would enable the legislation to be passed.
Budgets were delivered on a Thursday according to standing orders, he said.
